projectDesc.p: The Welte-Mignon Advertisements Collection brings together print advertisements for the Welte-Mignon reproducing piano that appeared between 1905 and 1930. It was created as part of the PhD project "Grünfelds Geist" at the University of Tübingen, which considers piano rolls as objects of a digital edition. The collection is published at https://anz.welte225.org.

samplingDecl.p: The collection gathers print advertisements for the Welte-Mignon reproducing piano that appeared between 1905 and 1930 and were published by M. Welte & Söhne, by one of its licensees, or by a dealer or agent selling the instrument. Each advertisement is encoded once; its further printings, in the same or in other periodicals, are listed as further sources.

The advertisements were found in digitised newspapers and magazines: Chronicling America (Library of Congress), the British Newspaper Archive, HathiTrust (copies of the Universities of California, Illinois, Michigan, Minnesota and Virginia), the Internet Archive, the Digitale Sammlungen of the Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, ANNO (Austrian National Library), the International Arcade Museum Library, Georgia Historic Newspapers, Delpher (KB, National Library of the Netherlands), eluxemburgensia (National Library of Luxembourg), RetroNews (Bibliothèque nationale de France), the archives of Le Temps, the Nasjonalbiblioteket of Norway, Mediestream (Royal Danish Library), the National Library of Latvia (through Europeana), Canadiana, the Hemeroteca Nacional Digital de México, the St Petersburg State Theatre Library, Trove (National Library of Australia), the newspapers of the Kungliga biblioteket of Sweden, e-newspaperarchives.ch, BAnQ numérique (Bibliothèque et Archives nationales du Québec), the Biblioteca Virtual de Prensa Histórica, the archive of ABC, ARCA (Biblioteca de Catalunya) and Polona (National Library of Poland).

editorialDecl.p: Each file transcribes one printing of an advertisement, the one whose scan its facsimile zones refer to; decls on text points to its sourceDesc. The further printings were identified as the same advertisement but not collated word for word; differences that were noticed are recorded with app or in a note.

The regions and lines of the scans were mostly marked in eScriptorium and converted from PAGE XML to TEI. The text was in part recognised automatically (HTR) and corrected against the scan, in part transcribed by hand. The advertisements published outside Germany, the United Kingdom and the United States, and a few from Germany, were transcribed from the scans, encoded, given their regions and annotated with topics by Claude, an AI model; their revision history says so. Until the editor has checked such an advertisement against the scan, status on its revisionDesc is unchecked; that of every other advertisement is checked.

correction.p: Errors of the original are not corrected but marked with sic.

normalization.p: Spelling and punctuation follow the original and are not normalised. Text set in capitals is often transcribed in mixed case and marked with the rendition #uc.

hyphenation.p: Hyphens at the end of a line are kept as printed.

segmentation.p: Every region of the original page is a div that points to its zone in the facsimile with facs. The lines of the original are marked with lb; the typography is recorded with rendition. The zones refer to the first graphic of a surface, the scan they were drawn on. Where the holding library serves the page through IIIF, a second graphic of the type IIIF gives that image and its size.

interpretation.p: Parts of an advertisement that concern other products than the Welte-Mignon are not transcribed but marked with gap, which describes them in a desc. Illustrations are described in figure. Persons are linked to the GND with corresp. Recurring motifs are marked as topics with ana on seg and figure, pointing to the taxonomy of topics; these are an interpretation, by whom resp says.

stdVals.p: Dates of publication are given in ISO 8601 in when, as precisely as they are known.

taxonomy.desc: Topics: recurring motifs of the advertisements, in their texts and in their pictures

ab.hi:
A really satisfactory way
to buy musical instruments

div.ab:
A FEELING of utter confidence is engendered at the
Welte-Mignon Studios. You instinctively know
that your continued patronage is sought and, therefore,
that everything will be made to bend toward
giving you thorough and complete
satisfaction. There is a wide range of
instruments from which to choose, at
prices and on terms thoroughly in
accord with your own idea of what is
equitable.

The instrument chosen by Paderewski, Lhe-
vinne,
Hofman , Busoni and scores of others, to
preserve their genius for posterity.
You should hear Paderewski's reproductions;
hear how
he has played his soul into indestructible records for the
Welte-Mignon .
Records which you may reproduce at any
time and as often as you like , in your own home.
One hundred and fifty-six
musicians have recorded more
than
five thousand
selections for the Welte-Mignon. Imagine
the delight to be derived from such a collection.
And con-
sider that the Welte-Mignon Reproducing Piano is within
everyone's means, for it may be bought on your terms, with-
in reason.
Just drop in at the Studios to hear the Welte play. Please
feel free to ask for your favorite selections. We consider the
pleasure entirely ours.

figure.desc: Woman sitting in a chair in front of an upright piano.

ab.hi:
We maintain that if music is to be enjoyed by every-
one, it must be within everyone's reach. So we placed every
instrument in the Studios just there–within EVERYONE'S
means. Pick out any instrument you like, from lowest to
highest in price, and buy it on YOUR OWN TERMS,
within reason.

gap.desc: The ad also includes texts for "Pathe", "Pianos and Player-Pianos" and "Victor Victrolas and Victor Records" which have been omitted here.
